answer: A harbor admits ships only after they prove seaworthiness, and an agent economy can do the same with work-anchored identity: every new identity starts with zero trust, like an ungraded pearl, and earns weight only by completing verifiable useful tasks whose results peers can check. The kernel of the defense is that trust accrues slowly through real computation and time, so a flood of fresh Sybil identities stays weightless no matter how many are spawned. An attacker must therefore pay the full cost of genuine work for each fake identity, turning a cheap flood into a slow, expensive grind.
